passages.title: The Kite That Would Not Fly
passages.text:
On Saturday morning, Anaya carried a bright paper kite to the open field near her home. Her grandfather had helped her make it from thin sticks, paper and string. Anaya was sure it would fly as soon as she ran.

She hurried across the grass and lifted the kite high. A light breeze moved the trees, but the kite tipped sideways and fell. Anaya tried again, pulling the string tightly. The kite dragged along the ground. She frowned and said that the kite must be broken.

Grandfather asked her to pause and look carefully. One corner of the paper had come loose from its frame, and the tail was shorter on one side than the other. Anaya fetched a small strip of paper and some tape. Together, they fixed the loose corner and made the tail even.

They waited for a steadier breeze. Grandfather explained that running too quickly could make it harder to notice how the kite responded to the wind. Anaya held the kite while he checked that the string was untangled. Then she walked forward slowly, letting the wind lift the kite before she gave the string a gentle pull.

This time, the kite rose above the field. It dipped once, but Anaya loosened the string a little and it climbed again. She watched its movements instead of pulling hard whenever it tilted. Soon the kite was high in the sky, its tail fluttering behind it.

Anaya wanted to tell everyone that she had made the kite fly by running faster. Grandfather reminded her of the repairs, the steadier breeze and the careful way she had handled the string. Anaya smiled. She had learned that a problem is easier to solve when you stop, observe the evidence and try a thoughtful change. On the way home, she decided to keep a small notebook of things she learned by testing ideas.
